source.quote: Soekris Engineering's own page for the dac1541, read 2026-11-25. The page states « The dac1541 is now discontinued ». On the ladder: « It have the fantastic clean and natural sound of a 27 bit R-2R sign magnitude DAC, built with over four hundred tiny and ultra precise thin film resistors. » Inputs: « SPDIF / AES / Toslink Inputs Up to 24 bit / 192 Khz »; « USB Input PCM Up to 24 Bit / 384 Ksps »; « USB Input DSD Up to DoP-128 and DSD-256 ». Filters: « with a set of selectable advanced digital filters ». The word NOS appears nowhere on the page.

facts.chip: « a 27 bit R-2R sign magnitude DAC, built with over four hundred tiny and ultra precise thin film resistors » - twice the resistor count of the current dac2541, at one bit less.

_verification_des_conditions_faite: soekris.dk links no terms page: the nav is Home, Products, Downloads, Ordering, About, Contact, and the footer reads « Copyright (c) 2023 Soekris Audio. » - the ordinary notice. About and Ordering were not opened, so a clause elsewhere is not formally excluded.
_le_mot_NOS_napparait_NULLE_PART_chez_ce: A discrete R-2R ladder is where one expects to find non-oversampling, and the reader checked every Soekris page read: « NOS does not appear in any Soekris page read. Nothing says 'non-oversampling' or 'oversampling'. » So `correctable` is NOT written, although the field's own definition says corrections exist « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM » and this is exactly the kind of converter that usually qualifies. The maker says « a set of selectable advanced digital filters » instead, which implies filters are IN the path. Writing correctable here from the topology would be inferring a behaviour from a circuit - the error the Nagra record was corrected for.
_un_modele_arrete_qui_merite_sa_fiche: The maker says it is discontinued and keeps the page up with its full specification. A device people own is a device an engine will meet, and the record exists for them. Same reasoning as the Cambridge CXN100, archived on its own maker's site and recorded here.
